native_sources.name: admin_notices
native_sources.notes: Ephemeral admin-screen notice substrate; not a durable per-user Notification Instance.

native_sources.name: Roles & Capabilities
native_sources.notes: Authorization/recipient input substrate only; canonical role truth remains delegated.

native_sources.name: WP-Cron
native_sources.notes: Scheduling substrate owned by the Cron/Job surface.

native_sources.name: wp_mail()
native_sources.notes: Email transport/output primitive owned by Surface 20, not Notifications.

records.label: Rule Identity / Name / Category / Lifecycle
records.notes: WordPress core has no persistent notification-rule Definition/lifecycle engine.

records.label: Typed Event / Registered Action Binding
records.notes: Reviewed typed adapters may wrap stable native lifecycle events; arbitrary authored hook names or executable callbacks remain forbidden.

records.label: Condition Engine Reference
records.notes: No native generic condition engine; references stay delegated to the canonical condition owner.

records.label: Recipient Resolution Policy
records.notes: Native users/roles are inputs only; recipient-resolution and fan-out semantics remain Notifications-owned.

records.label: Query / Role / Membership Recipient References
records.notes: Query, Roles and Membership are consumed read-only through canonical owner references.

records.label: Authorization / Preference / Quiet-Hours Eligibility
records.notes: Capabilities/session state are native authorization substrate; preferences and quiet hours are not a native notification engine.

records.label: Priority / Requiredness Classification
records.notes: WordPress core defines no generic notification priority/requiredness model.

records.label: In-App / Email / Webhook Channel Routing
records.notes: Admin/user/network notices are ephemeral native presentation channels only; durable inbox state is WPE-owned and Email/Webhook transports remain delegated to their canonical owners.

records.label: In-App Content / Allowlisted Token Schema
records.notes: No native persistent notification template/token schema exists.

records.label: Immediate / Delay / Date-Time / Timezone Policy
records.notes: WP-Cron is native scheduling substrate, but execution belongs to the Cron/Job owner and this surface does not schedule directly.

records.label: Dedupe / Frequency Cap Policy
records.notes: WordPress core has no notification dedupe/frequency-cap engine.

records.label: Digest / Grouping / Overflow Policy
records.notes: WordPress core has no durable notification digest/grouping engine.

records.label: Inbox Instance State / Expiry
records.notes: Core admin notices are request/screen rendering hooks, not durable per-user read/dismiss/expiry state.

records.label: Delivery State / Retry / Idempotency
records.notes: Acceptance/delivery evidence and retries are transport/provider-specific and remain cross-owner runtime concerns.

records.label: User Preferences / Retention / Health / Bounded Fan-Out
records.notes: Options/user meta may store bounded preference values, but core supplies no notification-preference product semantics.

records.label: Arbitrary Hook / Executable Callback
records.notes: Raw user-authored hook names/callbacks remain rejected; only registered typed event adapters may be referenced.

coverage.notes: Native audit provenance is integrated for admin/user/network notices, authorization inputs, WP-Cron and cross-owner mail transport. WordPress has no persistent Notifications rule/inbox engine; product and market semantics remain for later review and raw hooks stay rejected.
